name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention; accurately describes behavior (wait for keyboard input while repainting the in-battle field + mini-status overlay panel). No Ghidra address residue. The 'wait_input' + 'status_panel_repaint' descriptor matches the body: spins until fd2_check_keyboard_buffer_nonempty(), and each tick repaints field, cursor overlay, chars, mini-status panel, terrain HUD, then blits to screen.
purpose: Wait until keyboard input is available while continuously repainting the in-battle field and a mini-status overlay panel for runtime_char[char_idx]; does NOT consume the key (caller reads it afterward via fd2_wait_for_action_target_input).
logic_summary: Picks panel screen-side offset based on cursor screen X to avoid covering the cursor: panel_off = (data_fd2_battle_cursor_screen_x < 7) ? 0x984 (left) : 0x8ED (right). Then loops: while keyboard buffer is empty, calls fd2_update_palette_cycle_anim(); when BIOS tick word (0x46C) changes from last_tick, does a second palette-cycle update, ticks chapter palette animation, composites the battle tile map into the offscreen buffer (base+0x8088, stride 0x1C8) at the battle view window origin, paints the cursor/range overlay, composites all char sprites, renders the mini char status panel for char_idx at base+0x8088+panel_off, renders the terrain info HUD panel, blits the assembled 0x138x0xC0 region to VRAM 0xA0504 (stride 0x140), and latches last_tick. Returns when a key becomes available.

params.name: char_idx
params.semantics: Index into data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr of the character whose HP/MP is shown in the mini-status panel. Passed straight through (as param_1) by the sole caller fd2_player_action_menu_loop and forwarded unchanged to fd2_render_mini_char_status_panel.
params.reason: Name accurately reflects the runtime_char array index role and matches its forwarded use; no address residue, not a generic param_N name.

returns.semantics: No return value; loop simply exits once fd2_check_keyboard_buffer_nonempty() reports a pending key, which the caller then reads.
